1.why: The recovery token is stored in the requesting session's state and /api/recovery/reset-password requires state.recovery.accountRef === 'protected-account', binding the code to that session and account.

2.why: False — /api/recovery/verify only compares the submitted token against the current session's own state.recovery record, so the same code cannot be used from any other session or user.

3.why: True — the reset endpoint only flips flags on the current session and nothing revokes other entries in the sessions Map, so previously authenticated sessions remain usable until their 30-minute expiry.

4.why: The server listens exclusively over TLS, rejects non-https requests, and sets HSTS and upgrade-insecure-requests, though no explicit TLS version (e.g., minVersion) is configured.

5.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed and tokens are generated via crypto.getRandomValues, but reset codes and account data are stored unencrypted in the in-memory session Map rather than encrypted.

6.why: No email is implemented — delivery is simulated by returning mockDeliveryToken/mockRecoveryLink in the API response — so whether an email guards private data cannot be confirmed.

7.why: Identifiers must pass a strict regex, JSON bodies are type-checked, tokens are trimmed and length-checked, and the client renders all input via textContent under a nonce-based CSP.

8.why: All navigation uses history.pushState to same-origin '/?...' URLs with a whitelisted view set, the mock recovery link is same-origin, and no external redirect target exists anywhere.

9.why: No email templates exist in the system; separately, no user input is ever rendered as HTML (textContent only), so the claim is vacuous but not contradicted.

10.why: Error pages are generic with no stack traces, but the UI deliberately mirrors the working recovery token and MFA code into the on-page log panel and browser console.

11.why: Passwords are stored only as bcrypt hashes, but the MFA secret '246810' (MFA_TEST_CODE) and the mock recovery identifier are hardcoded directly in the source.

12.why: No default password exists, but the static hardcoded MFA code — which is even returned to the client as mockMfaCode — effectively functions as a default credential.

13.why: Both /api/recovery/verify and /api/mfa/verify block further attempts for 60 seconds after 5 failures via the registerFailure/blocked mechanism.

14.why: /api/recovery/request returns the identical generic message for every identifier; only the publicly documented demo value additionally receives mock delivery fields, so real account existence is not exposed.

15.why: The reset code is 32 bytes from crypto.getRandomValues encoded base64url, single-use, 10-minute TTL, and stored per-session, making it random, complex, and user/session-specific.
